title: The headline AI output speaks English inside a fully Czech workspace — the lang plumbing exists and is never passed on the group-eval path
expected: A Czech hiring manager (journey language: cs) reads the AI comparison headline, per-candidate verdicts/strengths/gaps/probes, risks, summary and governance note in Czech, like every other string in the modal.
got: Modal chrome is fully localized (messages/cs.json:1535-1622) but every generated/synthesized string is English: runReasoning is called without lang (defaults 'en'), group_compare_cli never passes lang to generate() though generate(lang=...) and language_directive exist, and the deterministic summary, risks and governance note are hardcoded English. The sealed rationale mirror also has no cs mapping for 'lead'/'advisory' reason codes.
suggested_acceptance: Pass the recruiter locale through the group_eval task (mirroring interview_prep at DecisionsTab.tsx:198-203) into runReasoning and a new --lang on group_compare_cli; localize or key the deterministic summary/risks/governance note; add cs mirrors for 'lead'/'advisory' reason codes.
l2_priority: Generate a real eval in a cs session and confirm what language the headline, verdicts and risks actually render in.

title: Headline ranking flat-sorts early-career (potential-scored) against experienced (history-scored) candidates — the engine's own module calls these scales incomparable and ships an unused track-grouped API
expected: The recommended order and lead either compare within fairness tracks (recruiter.py's rank_candidates_by_track contract) or the UI clearly separates/flags the two scales so the side-by-side is genuinely apples-to-apples (Tomas's trust criterion, Lucie's consistent-scoring DoD).
got: runGroupEval sorts the whole field on one `score` (ko-aware only); recruiter.py:87-89 warns 'a flat sort mixes incomparable scales' and provides rank_candidates_by_track (recruiter.py:93-103) which group-eval never uses. ComparisonTable labels each dimension row from the FIRST candidate that carries it, so one 'career' label spans potential-readiness and work-history-fit numbers. Mitigations exist (archetype tag, potential badge, early-career risk note, cross-scheme fairness matrix) but the ranking itself — the EU-AI-Act-high-risk artifact — is the mixed one. Affects Tomas equally (apples-to-apples criterion).
suggested_acceptance: Group or visually split the comparison by fairness track (the row `track` already rides every recruiter row), or at minimum label the career row per-candidate and annotate the recommended order when it crosses tracks.
l2_priority: Open a real eval on a mixed student+senior pool: check whether the career row label/values and the recommended order mislead, and whether the early-career risk note is enough.

title: When the whole field fails knockout, the comparison table still crowns column 1 with the Lead pill — contradicting the engine's own 'no lead' verdict on the same screen
expected: Journey DoD: 'the recommended lead actually passes the role's must-haves'. If no candidate passes KO, no one is crowned anywhere — the engine already refuses (lead=null, 'no lead' summary, nothing sealed).
got: CandidateHeader receives isLead={i === 0} unconditionally and checks isLead BEFORE the KO pill, so with an all-KO-failed (ko-aware-sorted) field the top column renders the crowned 'Lead' pill and its KO status is hidden, directly under a summary saying none pass the must-haves. Engine-side integrity (sort, crown, seal) is correct; the visual layer contradicts it.
suggested_acceptance: Drive isLead from the payload's topPick/lead (null when the field failed KO) instead of column index; a KO-failed first column shows the KO pill.
l2_priority: Seed a role where every pending candidate misses a must-have, run the eval, and screenshot the header row vs the summary.

title: Provenance stops at 'AI vs rule-based': no model/version identity anywhere, and the sealed group_eval_lead record carries only a 3-field inputs snapshot
expected: Lucie's criterion: every headline AI output carries model/version, inputs, timestamp and the authorizing human; the decision record snapshots 'the decisive inputs the decision actually saw' (the store's own contract).
got: Timestamp and source-class disclosure exist (subtitle + AI/rule pill), but the 'llm' source renders as a static 'Claude/Gemini' guess regardless of which provider actually ran; the sealed record's policyVersion is just 'llm|partial|deterministic' and inputs are {score, candidates, roleTitle} — no per-dimension breakdown, no KO status, no model id, and no reference (key/hash) linking the seal to the persisted group_evals payload that holds the full context.
suggested_acceptance: Carry the actual provider/model id (and prompt version, e.g. group-compare-v2 already emitted by the CLI) through the payload into the pill and the sealed record; add roleKey + eval createdAt (or a payload hash) and the lead's KO/dimension snapshot to inputs.
l2_priority: Export the dossier after a real eval and assess what a regulator would actually see for a group_eval_lead record.

title: Ranker failure degrades silently: fairness panel vanishes, knockout gating disappears (undefined = passed), yet a lead is still crowned and sealed
expected: Journey mandate: fairness 'fails open to deterministic, not silently off'. A run where the recruiter ranking failed should say so — and should not seal a lead whose must-haves were never checked.
got: The LLM weight-proposer layer does fail open with disclosure (rule-based-weights pill). But a whole-ranker failure is caught with console.warn only: fairness=null renders nothing (no notice), koPassed=undefined is treated as not-failed by the ko-aware sort and the lead gate, and the lead is crowned + sealed from stale matchScores. Only signal is the 'deterministic' source pill; the modal falls to LegacyView with no degraded-run warning.
suggested_acceptance: Persist a degraded:true flag when rankCandidates throws for a role WITH a job; the modal shows an explicit 'fairness/knockout not evaluated this run' notice, and the seal is skipped or marked unverified-KO in that state.
l2_priority: Optional (hard to force live): break the python env or point at a job-less role and confirm what the modal discloses about the degraded run.

title: Governance-mode selector applies only to the NEXT fresh run — opening a cached eval shows whatever mode it ran under, with no drift cue
expected: If the header selector says 'Komise (poradní)' and I open a role's evaluation, either the eval reflects committee mode or the modal tells me it was generated under a different mode.
got: evalMode is read only inside the fresh-run branch of openGroupEval; a cached eval renders its own stored governanceMode. In default recommendation mode there is no mode indicator at all in the modal, and the drift notice covers pool changes only — so a committee chair can read an auto-sealed AI recommendation believing advisory mode was active.
suggested_acceptance: Show the eval's governanceMode in the modal subtitle for all modes, and add a mode-mismatch notice (selector != payload.governanceMode) prompting a re-run.
l2_priority: Flip the selector to committee, open an already-evaluated role, and confirm what the user believes is happening.

title: 'Unique strengths (lead)' chips are keyed by display label while everything else was hardened to entryId — duplicate names mis-attribute the lead's edge
expected: The differentiator chips render only on the actual lead's tab, using the same stable-identity discipline (candIdentity/entryId) the decide path uses.
got: PerCandidateTabs matches topPick === c.label; topPick itself is persisted with label only (no entryId). Two same-named candidates in one role would both (or the wrong one) show the lead's unique strengths, while inline decide was explicitly fixed to key by entryId for this exact reason.
suggested_acceptance: Persist topPick.entryId and compare candIdentity(c) === topPick.entryId (label fallback for old payloads).

title: Ship-bar: group-eval store and decision chain are tenant-blind — on a multi-workspace deployment every workspace reads every bank's shortlist evals and decision dossiers
expected: group_evals and decision_records rows are scoped to a workspace/tenant, and the read routes enforce the caller's tenancy, before any public launch.
got: group_evals is keyed by role_key alone, decision_records has no tenant column, and GET /api/decisions/group-eval + GET /api/decisions/records perform no auth/tenant scoping — while real auth advertises multi-workspace tenancy (env.md). Demo-scoped today (dev gate), so live impact is near zero until launch; recorded as public-product-path evidence, not a current-user defect.
scope_note: Interview-case/demo scope — severity reflects the public product path, impact.reachability reflects today's dev-gated reality; ranks low until launch.
suggested_acceptance: Add workspace_id to both stores and scope the read routes by the session workspace before any multi-tenant deployment.

title: STRENGTH — Human oversight is architectural, not decorative: humans seal advance/reject/reinstate; the AI seals only a recommendation, and advisory modes never seal a winner
got: Advance/Reject always requires a human click, CAS-pinned, sealed as human:recruiter with an optional reason; reversal (reinstate) is sealed too; group-eval seals group_eval_lead as a recommendation record, and committee/eligibility modes structurally prevent an AI-sealed winner with an honest ceiling note about statutory preferences. This directly answers GDPR Art. 22 / AI Act human-oversight design at L1.
suggested_acceptance: Protect this: any future 'auto-advance the lead' feature must keep the human seal in the path.

title: STRENGTH — The fairness panel names its own ceiling (weighting robustness, NOT demographic bias) and discloses its weight source; the compliance surface pairs it with a jurisdiction-aware four-fifths calculator
got: Cross-scheme matrix re-scores every candidate under every candidate's bounded weighting with per-candidate rationales and a divergence callout; the scope note states plainly it does not assess protected-class bias because the app holds no such data; AI-tuned vs rule-based weights are labelled; the Rules modal adds an honest covered-vs-ceiling posture and an in-browser four-fifths check that stores nothing.
suggested_acceptance: Keep the scope note verbatim through any redesign — it is the single most defensible sentence on the surface.
l2_priority: Confirm the matrix + weight notes render on a real mixed pool and the keyless run shows the rule-based pill.

title: STRENGTH — Decide-in-context with honest state: inline Advance/Reject at the point of maximum comparison, id-keyed, CAS-guarded, never faking success on stale entries
got: The modal's decide resolves candidate identity to the live pipeline entry by id (label fallback for old payloads), reuses the queue's expectedStage CAS so a stale decision 409s instead of overriding another actor, and only flips to the outcome pill when the action actually landed. Coverage honesty (top-N-of-M note) and pool-drift warnings keep a cached eval from silently lying.
suggested_acceptance: Protect the CAS + no-fake-success pattern when adding bulk actions.

title: STRENGTH — Currency-honest salary comparison: cross-currency expectations are withheld from the LLM and excluded from the shared bar scale instead of enabling a false over/under-budget claim
got: The compare context only hands the LLM a salary midpoint when it shares the band's currency (the app does no FX), and the table excludes cross-currency expectations from the shared scale, showing an explicit 'not comparable' note instead of plotting a meaningless bar. Differentiators are likewise constrained to declared role requirements the lead matched and every rival missed — never off-topic self-claims.
suggested_acceptance: Keep the withhold-on-mismatch rule if FX support ever lands half-way.
